Planning, fit and risk register

ProjectBuyer fitComparison riskFuture context
Emerald Of KatongSubject benchmarkBuyers seeking a new family project near Tanjong Katong MRT at a leasehold quantumLaunch-period caveats dominate and resale evidence is not yet matureThe Thomson-East Coast Line is operating context; future area plans are not added to achieved prices
Tembusu GrandLeasehold launch controlBuyers comparing a completed leasehold product with recent sub-sale evidenceNew-sale and sub-sale records are not interchangeable with established resaleCompletion changes the buyer decision but does not remove sale-state selection effects
Grand DunmanMega-project controlHouseholds prioritising scale and Dakota MRT accessIts Dakota micro-market and larger stock differ from the Jalan Tembusu subjectsPipeline supply and completion timing are context rather than realised price uplift
The ContinuumFreehold launch controlBuyers accepting a higher PSF for freehold tenure and a central Katong locationFreehold tenure and dual-site design make pooled medians misleadingCompare achieved transactions by bedroom and sale state before reading a tenure premium
Katong RegencyMixed-use freehold controlBuyers prioritising retail and rail convenience over a coastal micro-locationSmall stock and thin samples can move medians sharplyPaya Lebar context differs from the Jalan Tembusu and Amber clusters
Haig CourtLarge-format freehold controlSpace-seeking households willing to accept an older projectAge condition and large unit sizes confound headline quantum and PSF comparisonsUse size and floor filters before drawing conclusions from its freehold status
The Shore ResidencesLeasehold location controlBuyers valuing established East Coast Road amenities and a completed homeIts lease structure and completed resale state differ from current launchesOperating TEL access is present context and should not be treated as future uplift
One AmberAmber freehold controlBuyers comparing mature freehold stock with current Katong launchesSea-facing dispersion and older completion can dominate project-level mediansCoastal amenity access is a liveability consideration rather than a standalone price adjustment

Sources and calculation register

Transaction and method sources

  • URA private residential transaction search — achieved caveats, latest 60 months.
  • URA REALIS coverage and methodology — caveat coverage limitations.
  • Headline window: 2025-01–2026-06; growth windows: 2024-07–2025-06 and 2025-07–2026-06.
  • Bedroom labels retain their source field. MRT and school diagnostics are coordinate-derived and not official walking or home-school distances.

Project fact sources

  • Emerald Of Katong project facts — 99-year leasehold, 846 units, Expected 2028.
  • Tembusu Grand project facts — 99-year lease from 2022, 638 units, Completed 2025.
  • Grand Dunman project facts — 99-year leasehold, 1,008 units, Expected 2028.
  • The Continuum project facts — Freehold, 816 units, Expected 2026.
  • Katong Regency project facts — Freehold, 244 units, Completed 2015.
  • Haig Court project facts — Freehold, 360 units, Completed 2004.
  • The Shore Residences project facts — 103-year lease from 2009, 408 units, Completed 2014.
  • One Amber project facts — Freehold, 562 units, Completed 2010.
Research limitations. URA caveats are voluntary and not exhaustive. Bedroom labels use a secondary row-match layer because the public URA transaction extract does not publish bedrooms. Project coordinates, MRT distance and school counts are diagnostics, not official eligibility measurements. New sale, sub-sale and resale have different price-setting conditions. No asking prices, rental yields or estate-level Provision scores are blended into a project ranking.
